arxiv-2112-09478.title: Free-Riding for Future: Field Experimental Evidence of Strategic Substitutability in Climate Protest Thanks: The research for this article has been funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy, cluster EXC 2037 “CLICCS: Climate,
arxiv-2112-09478.creator: Johannes Jarke-Neuert, Grischa Perino, Henrike Schwickert
arxiv-2112-09478.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Johannes Jarke-Neuert, Grischa Perino, Henrike Schwickert. We test the hypothesis that protest participation decisions in an adult population of potential climate protesters are interdependent. Subjects ( n = 1,510 n=1,510 ) from the four largest German cities were recruited two weeks before protest date.

arxiv-2209-03480.title: Geodesic Convexity of the Symmetric Eigenvalue Problem and Convergence of Riemannian Steepest Descent
arxiv-2209-03480.creator: Foivos Alimisis Bart Vandereycken
arxiv-2209-03480.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Foivos Alimisis Bart Vandereycken. We study the convergence of the Riemannian steepest descent algorithm on the Grassmann manifold for minimizing the block version of the Rayleigh quotient of a symmetric matrix. Even though this problem is non-convex in the Euclidean sense and only very locally convex in the Riemannian sense, we discover a structure for this problem that is similar to geodesic strong convexity, namely, weak-strong convexity.

arxiv-2305-16537.title: Functional equations and gamma factors of local zeta functions for the metaplectic cover of SL 2 {\rm SL}_{2}
arxiv-2305-16537.creator: Kazuki Oshita, Masao Tsuzuki
arxiv-2305-16537.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kazuki Oshita, Masao Tsuzuki. We introduce a local zeta-function for an irreducible admissible supercuspidal representation π \pi of the metaplectic double cover of SL 2 \mathrm{SL}_{2} over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We prove a functional equation of the local zeta-functions showing that the gamma factor is given by a Mellin type transform of the Bessel function of π \pi . We obtain an expression of the gamma factor, which shows its entireness on ℂ {\mathbb{C}} .

arxiv-2310-11372.title: 3D Force and Contact Estimation for a Soft-Bubble Visuotactile Sensor Using FEM
arxiv-2310-11372.creator: Jing-Chen Peng, Shaoxiong Yao, Kris Hauser, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2310-11372.description: Abstract Soft-bubble tactile sensors have the potential to capture dense contact and force information across a large contact surface. However, it is difficult to extract contact forces directly from observing the bubble surface because local contacts change the global surface shape significantly due to membrane mechanics and air pressure.

arxiv-2310-14803.title: Polarised cross sections for vector boson production with S HERPA
arxiv-2310-14803.creator: Mareen Hoppe, Marek Schönherr, Frank Siegert
arxiv-2310-14803.description: Abstract IPPP/23/60, MCNET-23-11 1 Introduction The investigation of the polarisation of massive vector bosons (VB) has gained significant attention in recent years, both theoretically and experimentally. The longitudinal polarisation of massive VBs is a direct consequence of the electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism, making polarised VB production a very promising group of processes for probing this mechanism.

arxiv-2506-07088.title: Pointwise confidence estimation in the non-linear ℓ 2 \ell^{2} -regularized least squares
arxiv-2506-07088.creator: Ilja Kuzborskij, Yasin Abbasi Yadkori
arxiv-2506-07088.description: Abstract We consider a high-probability non-asymptotic confidence estimation in the ℓ 2 \ell^{2} -regularized non-linear least-squares setting with fixed design. In particular, we study confidence estimation for local minimizers of the regularized training loss. We show a pointwise confidence bound, meaning that it holds for the prediction on any given fixed test input x x .

pmc-11522800.title: Exopeptidase combination enhances the degradation of isotopically labelled gluten immunogenic peptides in humans
pmc-11522800.creator: Sulayman Mourabit, Sarah Römer, Erin R. Bonner, Fabian Winter, Julian Tschollar, Mladen V. Tzvetkov, Werner Weitschies, Stefan Engeli, Werner Tschollar
pmc-11522800.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionCeliac disease is a common autoimmune-like enteropathy caused by an aberrant response to incompletely digested dietary gluten. Gluten immunogenic peptides including the immunodominant 33-mer are thought to be resistant to proteolytic digestion by human gastrointestinal peptidases. We developed a novel enzyme therapy approach to support gluten peptide digestion using a combination of two tandem-acting exopeptidases, AMYNOPEP, that complement the intrinsic enzymatic activity of intestinal brush border enterocytes.MethodsWe evaluated the effects of AMYNOPEP supplementation on 33-mer degradation in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-13105896.title: Multidisciplinary team management is associated with improved patient-centered outcomes in multiple pulmonary nodules: a prospective observational cohort study
pmc-13105896.creator: Tiantian Yuan, Lijuan Yuan, Zhimei Wang, Lijuan Cui, Rongmei Song, Yun Wang
pmc-13105896.description: BackgroundMultiple pulmonary nodules (MPNs) present diagnostic and management challenges, causing patient anxiety and inconsistent clinical recommendations. pmc-13643550.description: BackgroundUnicuspid aortic valve (UAV) is a rare congenital anomaly and is often misdiagnosed as a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). pmc-13680528.description: Ship recycling plays a central role in the circular economy of the maritime industry, yet significant disparities persist in safety, environmental performance, and regulatory compliance across global Ship Recycling Facilities (SRFs).
